[Codegen][CPU] Add RISC-V V bf16 vfwmaccbf16 inner_tiled MMA. (#25120)

(+zvfbfwma). N is vlen/8. Reuses `lowerRiscvVFmaccLike`. The spacemit

commit_message:
[CI] Run zizmor in pre-commit and fix workflow findings (#25225)

Lint workflow to checkGitHub Actions workflows.

Run [zizmor](https://docs.zizmor.sh/) from pre-commit, and fix zizimor
findings.

### Changes

- **Template injection:** run steps no longer expand `${{ inputs.* }}`,
`${{ github.event.inputs.* }}` or `${{ env.* }}` directly into the
script. Each value goes through the step's `env:` and is used as a
quoted shell variable.
- **Checkout token on disk :** checkouts set `persist-credentials:
false`.
- **`secrets: inherit`:** ci.yml, pkgci.yml and samples.yml pass each
reusable workflow only the secrets it declares under `workflow_call`.

- **Other findings:**
- Dependabot waits seven days before it proposes a new action release.
Security updates are not delayed.
- publish_website.yml runs on `release` and pushes to gh-pages, so it no
longer restores a pip cache that other workflows on main can write
(zizimor: cache-poisoning)
- Three pin comments named a release that did not match the pinned
commit.
- pull_request_greeter.yml keeps `pull_request_target`, marked as
reviewed: it runs only base-branch code and passes PR fields through
`env`.
- The candidate release workflows keep ncipollo/release-action, because
build_package.yml needs the draft release id it outputs.
- **Hook:** zizmor v1.32.0, pinned to a commit.

---------

Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[CI] Run zizmor in pre-commit and fix workflow findings (#25225)

Lint workflow to checkGitHub Actions workflows.

Run [zizmor](https://docs.zizmor.sh/) from pre-commit, and fix zizimor
findings.

### Changes

- **Template injection:** run steps no longer expand `${{ inputs.* }}`,
`${{ github.event.inputs.* }}` or `${{ env.* }}` directly into the
script. Each value goes through the step's `env:` and is used as a
quoted shell variable.
- **Checkout token on disk :** checkouts set `persist-credentials:
false`.
- **`secrets: inherit`:** ci.yml, pkgci.yml and samples.yml pass each
reusable workflow only the secrets it declares under `workflow_call`.

- **Other findings:**
- Dependabot waits seven days before it proposes a new action release.
Security updates are not delayed.
- publish_website.yml runs on `release` and pushes to gh-pages, so it no
longer restores a pip cache that other workflows on main can write
(zizimor: cache-poisoning)
- Three pin comments named a release that did not match the pinned
commit.
- pull_request_greeter.yml keeps `pull_request_target`, marked as
reviewed: it runs only base-branch code and passes PR fields through
`env`.
- The candidate release workflows keep ncipollo/release-action, because
build_package.yml needs the draft release id it outputs.
- **Hook:** zizmor v1.32.0, pinned to a commit.

---------

Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Lint workflow to checkGitHub Actions workflows.

Run [zizmor](https://docs.zizmor.sh/) from pre-commit, and fix zizimor
findings.

### Changes

- **Template injection:** run steps no longer expand `${{ inputs.* }}`,
`${{ github.event.inputs.* }}` or `${{ env.* }}` directly into the
script. Each value goes through the step's `env:` and is used as a
quoted shell variable.
- **Checkout token on disk :** checkouts set `persist-credentials:
false`.
- **`secrets: inherit`:** ci.yml, pkgci.yml and samples.yml pass each
reusable workflow only the secrets it declares under `workflow_call`.

- **Other findings:**
- Dependabot waits seven days before it proposes a new action release.
Security updates are not delayed.
- publish_website.yml runs on `release` and pushes to gh-pages, so it no
longer restores a pip cache that other workflows on main can write
(zizimor: cache-poisoning)
- Three pin comments named a release that did not match the pinned
commit.
- pull_request_greeter.yml keeps `pull_request_target`, marked as
reviewed: it runs only base-branch code and passes PR fields through
`env`.
- The candidate release workflows keep ncipollo/release-action, because
build_package.yml needs the draft release id it outputs.
- **Hook:** zizmor v1.32.0, pinned to a commit.

---------

Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Lint workflow to checkGitHub Actions workflows.

Run [zizmor](https://docs.zizmor.sh/) from pre-commit, and fix zizimor
findings.

### Changes

- **Template injection:** run steps no longer expand `${{ inputs.* }}`,
`${{ github.event.inputs.* }}` or `${{ env.* }}` directly into the
script. Each value goes through the step's `env:` and is used as a
quoted shell variable.
- **Checkout token on disk :** checkouts set `persist-credentials:
false`.
- **`secrets: inherit`:** ci.yml, pkgci.yml and samples.yml pass each
reusable workflow only the secrets it declares under `workflow_call`.

- **Other findings:**
- Dependabot waits seven days before it proposes a new action release.
Security updates are not delayed.

longer restores a pip cache that other workflows on main can write
(zizimor: cache-poisoning)

commit.
- pull_request_greeter.yml keeps `pull_request_target`, marked as
reviewed: it runs only base-branch code and passes PR fields through
`env`.
- The candidate release workflows keep ncipollo/release-action, because
build_package.yml needs the draft release id it outputs.
- **Hook:** zizmor v1.32.0, pinned to a commit.

commit_message:
[Codegen] Don't hoist statically-bound allocations with bogus huge bounds

hoistOneStaticallyBoundAllocation used the result of computeConstantBound
verbatim as the static dimension of a hoisted alloca. An unconstrained
`index` operand carries the trivial type-level upper bound (2^53 - 1), so a
single `affine.apply` (e.g. `ceildiv 2`) turns it into a ~2^52-element static
`memref.alloca` (~16 PiB), emitted silently. Downstream stride/size math then
overflows i64 and the dispatch reads/writes undefined memory.

Refuse to hoist when the product of the constant bounds exceeds a generous
element-count cap (2^32), leaving the allocation dynamic, which is always
valid. Scalable bounds are skipped in the product (vscale >= 1, so it is still
a lower bound). The cap is intentionally backend-agnostic rather than the
target's max_stack_allocation_size: the stack check still enforces the real
limit downstream on LLVMCPU, and a budget-based cap would stop hoisting
legitimately large tiles when that check is disabled.

Fixes #24483.

commit_message:
[Runtime] Profile all devices in multi-device tool runs

iree-run-module, iree-run-mlir, iree-check-module and the e2e test
runners create one HAL device per `--device` flag, but began
profiling only on the first one. With `--device=A --device=B`, the
profile bundle and `--print_device_statistics` silently missed all
work on B.

The fix runs profiling on the whole device list instead, as
iree-benchmark-module already does. Single-device runs were not
changed and runs without HAL devices still skip profiling.

I left iree-benchmark-executable unchanged since it only ever
creates one device.

The existing two-device iree-run-module test and a new two-device
iree-check-module test now run with `--print_device_statistics`
and check that a dispatch from each device is reported.

Assisted-by: Claude Code
Signed-off-by: Zmicier Prybysh <zprybysh@baylibre.com>

iree-run-module, iree-run-mlir, iree-check-module and the e2e test
runners create one HAL device per `--device` flag, but began
profiling only on the first one. With `--device=A --device=B`, the
profile bundle and `--print_device_statistics` silently missed all
work on B.

The fix runs profiling on the whole device list instead, as
iree-benchmark-module already does. Single-device runs were not
changed and runs without HAL devices still skip profiling.

I left iree-benchmark-executable unchanged since it only ever
creates one device.

The existing two-device iree-run-module test and a new two-device
iree-check-module test now run with `--print_device_statistics`
and check that a dispatch from each device is reported.

Assisted-by: Claude Code
Signed-off-by: Zmicier Prybysh <zprybysh@baylibre.com>
name: linux_x64_clang_ubsan / linux_x64_clang_ubsan

commit_message:
[Runtime] Profile all devices in multi-device tool runs

iree-run-module, iree-run-mlir, iree-check-module and the e2e test
runners create one HAL device per `--device` flag, but began
profiling only on the first one. With `--device=A --device=B`, the
profile bundle and `--print_device_statistics` silently missed all
work on B.

The fix runs profiling on the whole device list instead, as
iree-benchmark-module already does. Single-device runs were not
changed and runs without HAL devices still skip profiling.

I left iree-benchmark-executable unchanged since it only ever
creates one device.

The existing two-device iree-run-module test and a new two-device
iree-check-module test now run with `--print_device_statistics`
and check that a dispatch from each device is reported.

commit_message:
[Codegen][CPU] Add RISC-V V bf16 vfwmaccbf16 inner_tiled MMA. (#25120)

Lower MMA_RISCV_V_VFWMACCBF16_*_F32_BF16 to llvm.riscv.vfwmaccbf16
(+zvfbfwma). N is vlen/8. Reuses `lowerRiscvVFmaccLike`. The spacemit
X60 board I have does not advertise zvfbwma, so didn't collect
performance numbers. The other dtypes are being tracked here: #24932

Correctness: a 64x64 ones matmul matched exactly under QEMU 8.1.2
(vlen=256, x-zvfbfwma). Lit covers VLEN 128/256/512 and the narrow-N
tile.
